etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English ille (“evil; wicked”), from Old Norse illr (adj), illa (adverb), ilt (noun) (whence Icelandic illur, Norwegian ille, Danish ilde), from Proto-Germanic *ilhilaz, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁elḱ- (whence Latin ulcus (“sore”), Ancient Greek ἕλκος (hélkos, “wound, ulcer”), Sanskrit अर्शस् (árśas, “hemorrhoids”).

quote.citation: 1709 December 6, Francis Atterbury, A Sermon Preached before the Sons of the Clergy, at their Anniversary-Meeting, in the Church of St. Paul:
quote.text: St. Paul chose to magnify his office when ill men conspired to lessen it.

quote.citation: 1749, Henry Fielding, The History of Tom Jones, a Foundling, volume (please specify |volume=I to VI), London: A[ndrew] Millar, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: A man who is conscious of having an ill character, cannot justly be angry with those who neglect and slight him.

definitions.definition: (archaic) Morally reprehensible (of behaviour etc.); blameworthy. [from 13th c.]

quote.citation: 1999, George R.R. Martin, A Clash of Kings, Bantam, published 2011, page 2:
quote.text: ‘Go bring her. It is ill to keep a lady waiting.’

definitions.definition: Indicative of unkind or malevolent intentions; harsh, cruel. [from 14th c.]
Unpropitious, unkind, faulty, not up to reasonable standard.

quote.text: […] his lordship was out of humour. That was the way Chollacombe described as knaggy an old gager as ever Charles had had the ill-fortune to serve. Stiff-rumped, that's what he was, always rubbing the rust, or riding grub, like he had been for months past.

definitions.definition: Unwell in terms of health or physical condition; sick. [from 15th c.]
Having an urge to vomit. [from 20th c.]

quote.text: Biggie Smalls is the illest / Your style is played out, like Arnold wonderin "Whatchu talkin bout, Willis?"

definitions.definition: (slang) Extremely bad (bad enough to make one ill). Generally used indirectly with to be.

quote.text: Oh that when the devil and flesh entice the sinner to sport with and make a mock of sin, Prov. x. 23, he would but consider, it is ill jesting with edged tools, it is ill jesting with unquenchable burnings;  […]
